body:
Merged `origin/main` (6349a542e) into the branch. The branch also merges cleanly with 1d103b265. New head: `458e8be2eeecdda6cf0ee1a379df6c95985219b2` (merge 9b599e8da plus follow-up 458e8be2e). No rebase and no force-push.

Conflicting files and resolutions:
- `crates/motion/src/machining3d/entry.rs` (hand-merged logic): main's `cut_levels_under(top_z, approach.stock_top, ...)` ladder law (#2004) is kept. The PR's extra `ladder` stock argument is kept. The new `pocket3d_open_prev` of this PR also uses `cut_levels_under` now, not `cut_levels`. Its doc says it is `pocket3d_prev` move for move, and main changed `pocket3d_prev` to `cut_levels_under`. With no `stock_top`, the two laws give the same levels.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/mod.rs` and `raster.rs` (keep both): the PR side had committed CRLF line ends, which made a whole-file conflict. I normalised the PR side to LF and did a three-way merge. The merge was clean. Main's `mod rest`, the `rest` re-exports and `mod conservative` are kept.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/air_links.rs`: CRLF changed to LF. The content did not change.

Follow-up commit 458e8be2e (compile fixes after the merge, no logic change):
- `machining3d/descent.rs`: main's new `find_clear_helix` (c505b2ed3) uses `along_pass`, `lattice`, `disc_clears`, `dive_room` and `bore_meets_lifted_leg`. This PR had moved or stopped importing these items. I added the imports again. Main did not change the code that this PR moved to `descent_place.rs`.
- `crates/motion/tests/pocket3d_mask_edge.rs` (a new test from main): `open_sides` now takes `stock_band`. The calls pass `stock_band(r, false)`, which equals the old band `r - OPEN_SLACK`. No assertion, golden or pinned count changed.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` passed: 322 steps, 0 failed (wall time 61.7 min). The steps include all of the motion suites, the app lib and app suites (including `pocket3d_air_band`, `pocket3d_hsm`, `pocket3d_open_side`, `golden_cl`, `adaptive_fig8_crossing` and `top_z_stock_over`) and the ui suites. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

The first gate run stopped because of the compile errors above. A second run was killed by a shell timeout during the app build, which the gate reported as a compile error. A plain `cargo test -p camcraft-app --no-run --tests` built without errors.

This is a DELTA refresh (hunks resolved by hand), so it needs a delta review. The work is under the safety floor.

ready for a re-check

Quick pass on head `458e8be2e`: the PR merges cleanly with `main`. The author's quick gate is green on this head (322 steps, 0 failed, with `golden_cl`, `top_z_stock_over` and the `pocket3d_*` suites). The refresh comment names the hand-merged hunks. I flag the PR ready for a delta review under the safety floor.

Read-only safety-floor review (Opus, diff only, not built) of the merged head 458e8be2eeecdda6cf0ee1a379df6c95985219b2.

Verdict: findings

I read the generator logic and the refusals in full: `air_rings.rs`, `air_chain.rs`, `air_links.rs`, `air_uncross.rs`, `pocket_hsm.rs`, `machining3d/{hsm,ladder,entry,open_side,descent}.rs` and `app/src/operation/{generate,open_side}.rs`. I read the tests by name and assert lines only.

## Findings

1. **defect** - `crates/motion/src/machining3d/hsm.rs:234-237` and `crates/motion/src/machining3d/ladder.rs:195`.
   `plan_level` adds the note `AIR_ENTRY` ("the level is entered by a plunge in the air outside the stock") when `in_air` holds. It does not look at the tool. The ladder then sets `air: lp.air_entry && p.links.approach.center_cutting`. For a tool that is not centre-cutting, the ladder uses the old entry law, but the note still says that a plunge in the air occurred. The posted program and the note do not agree. This is a misleading message, not a wrong move. Fix: add the note only where the ladder takes the air entry (or test `center_cutting` in `plan_level`). No test pins the note for a tool that is not centre-cutting.

2. **defect** - `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_hsm.rs:152`, `the_users_whole_model_bore_roughs_adaptive_on_each_level`.
   The ignore reason calls this test a "heavy lane" test of the release tier. It asserts that no level of the D plate falls to the Offset rings (`fell.is_empty()`). The PR body says that the D plate stock ring level still goes to the Offset rings (hop budget). Its debug twin `pocket_hsm::ring_tests::the_stock_ring_level_reaches_the_air_planner_with_the_stock` is ignored as red ("blocked after round H"). The PR did not run the heavy test. Thus the release tier at the next cut will very probably be red on this test. The ignore reason must say that the test is blocked on issue 1950 (as the twin says), or the assert must change. I did not run the test, so this is an expectation from the PR's own readings.

3. **note** - `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/air_rings.rs:160-165` with `leads` (line 338 and after).
   On a chain, the lead-in starts at `p[j]` on the previous pass, up to `LEAD_START_W` (4) load widths from the run. The first lead chord `p[j] -> q` has two end points in `center`. No `chord_clears(center, ..)` test is done on the chord itself. `air_chain::link` and `air_links::lead_of` do this test; this path does not. A run starts where a front meets the part wall, so `center` can be concave there (a convex part corner). The chord can then leave `center` by a small sag. The post gate's part check is the second line, so the result is a refusal, not a silent gouge. Recommend the same `chord_clears` test as `link`, with a fall back to the hop.

4. **note** - `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs:846` and `crates/app/src/operation/open_side.rs` (`air_band_refusal`).
   For each whole-model Adaptive 3D Pocket (not shell, not rest roughing), the tool disc now goes up to 2 tool radii past the stock side, on each level down to the bottom. Before, it stayed in the stock outline. Only a tagged fixture box refuses this. A vise or clamp that is not modelled is not seen. The changelog row says this, but a user who holds the stock in a vise without a fixture model can get a collision that the program cannot detect. Recommend a maintainer decision: an op parameter for the band (default off, or default on with a clear warning). This is a design choice, so it is not a defect here.

5. **note** - `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/air_rings.rs:84`.
   `open_air(stock.offset(4r) - stock)` marks as open all cells outside the stock, also the cells of the part (where the part is larger than the stock) and of neighbour parts. The load reading and `disc_clear` then read those cells as air. No gouge follows, because each point is held in `center`. But a reading near such a part is not true. Recommend `open_air` of the air less the part and the keep-out.

## Checks with no finding

- No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` outside tests in the new code. The index math is guarded: runs are filtered to two points or more, `Kept::split` gives pieces of two points or more, `loops()[0]` is behind `len() == 1`, `p[j]` comes from `onto` within bounds, the cell casts test `is_finite` and a bound.
- Loops are capped: `MAX_FRONTS`, `LEAD_TRIES`, `LEAD_PER_R`, `MAX_SPAN`.
- The load refusal holds: the worst of the passes, the run ends and the re-read joins is compared to the bound, and an over plan returns no passes and a named fallback. `adaptive_passes` still runs `first_crossing`, the rest law and the budgets on the air plan.
- `open_sides` keeps the old band for each other strategy with the same computation. A band under the open band is an error.
- The air entry plunge is taken only where `in_air` proves the disc clear of the stock outline by `r + 0.005`.
- The earlier review's notes 3 to 5 are correct as written.

## Not checked

- I did not build or run a test.
- I did not read `raster/walk.rs`, `descent_place.rs` or the `raster.rs` move line by line. I read the diff stat and the moved hunks only.
- I did not check `LinkLaw` (`lift_link.rs`), which this PR calls but does not change.
- I did not check the decision file against the code.
